title: Lesson 24: Measuring What's Working: Time Saved, Quality, and Adoption
description: Replacing trust with a short, honest measurement of one workflow: a baseline taken before the change, decision metrics rather than decoration, and adoption as steady use instead of a single try.

questions.question: Per the lesson "Measuring What's Working: Time Saved, Quality, and Adoption", what is a decision metric?
options: A number you would actually change your behavior on, as opposed to decoration
Any number that is easy to collect automatically
A metric that leadership has requested
The total number of tasks run in a month
questions.explanation: The lesson calls a count of tasks run decoration if you would keep running them regardless, and contrasts it with a number like drafting time dropping from nine minutes to five.

questions.question: Why does the lesson insist on taking a baseline?
options: Because baselines are required for compliance reporting
Because you cannot claim a tool saves time unless you know how long the task took before the tool existed, and skipping this is the biggest reason time-saved claims fall apart
Because a baseline replaces the need for a quality bar
Because it means you can skip measuring after the change
questions.explanation: The lesson says you measure first, then change, then measure again, and the difference is your answer, with the skipped baseline named as the reason the time-saved claims collapse.

questions.question: The lesson measures one workflow on three axes. Which set does it name?
questions.explanation: The lesson replaces trust with numbers on exactly those three axes so the team can tell whether to keep the workflow, fix it, or drop it.
